statement: Aishah: when healthy he said no prophet is taken until shown his place in Paradise and given the choice; at the end, his head on her thigh, he looked to the ceiling and said 'O Allah, with the highest companion'; she understood he would not choose them; these were his last words.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against both. That these were his last words is in the remainder of 4463, from memory.

statement: Aishah: he died in her house on her day against her chest; her brother Abd ar-Rahman entered with a siwak, she softened it and he used it; he dipped his hands in water, wiped his face and said 'la ilaha illa Allah, death has its agonies'.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the first part; the water and the words are in the remainder, from memory.

statement: He died on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal of year 11.
alternatives: Monday is established (Bukhari 680). The date is commonly given as 12 Rabi' al-Awwal; scholars have questioned that date on calendar grounds and some give the 1st or 2nd. The script states no day.

statement: Anas: Fatimah's words of mourning, and her question to Anas after the burial.
Umar stood and swore that the Messenger of Allah had not died; he later said nothing else had entered his mind.

Abu Bakr came on his horse from as-Sunh, entered without speaking to anyone, went to the Prophet who was covered with a striped cloak, uncovered his face, kissed him and wept, saying 'may my father and mother be your ransom; you were good in life and in death'.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against all three.

statement: Abu Bakr went out, told Umar to sit, praised Allah and said 'whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is living and does not die'; Ibn Abbas: it was as if people had not known the verse until he recited it; Umar: his legs gave way and he knew the Prophet had died.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for Abu Bakr's words; the statements of Ibn Abbas and Umar are in the remainder of 4454, from memory.
The narration also has him recite 39:30.

statement: Aishah: they did not know whether to remove his garments for washing; he was washed in his garment with water poured over it.
notes: Machine-checked for the opening; graded hasan. The voice heard from the side of the house, mentioned in the narration, is not narrated.

statement: People prayed over him in successive groups without an imam.
notes: Reported by Ibn Ishaq and in Ibn Majah 1628 (chain graded weak by some); narrated with attribution.

statement: He was buried where he died, in Aishah's room beside the mosque.
notes: Undisputed fact. The day of burial (Tuesday night into Wednesday) and the selection of Abu Bakr as caliph before it are not narrated.

statement: Anas: the day he entered Madinah everything in it was lit; the day he died everything in it was dark.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked; graded sahih (al-Albani, Ahmad Shakir).
